description: "Our NASA Space Apps project tackles cosmic and Earth challenges by turning open-source satellite data into actionable solutions. By bridging aerospace engineering and advanced data analytics, we engineered an intuitive, scalable tool designed to empower researchers, explore planetary systems, and inspire the next generation of space innovators."
summary:
"Mission Architect" is an interactive space mission design game and simulation developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It bridges the gap between theoretical space science and practical systems engineering by placing players in the shoes of a NASA systems engineer.
Players must design complete space missions, manage critical resources (such as mass, power, budget, and communications), and balance complex engineering trade-offs. The game features three distinct, meticulously designed mission scenarios:
 - Lunar Outpost: A human-crewed surface mission focusing on rover deployment, geological sampling, and long-duration exploration.
 - Martian Red Ridge: A robotic astrobiology mission to search for ancient microbial life, cache rock samples, and test atmospheric landing systems.
 - Venus Flagship Explorer: A multi-platform robotic mission utilizing an orbiter, atmospheric aerobot balloon, and a surface lander to study extreme environments.

By combining 3D interactive visualizations, real-time telemetry dashboards, and realistic constraint management, Mission Architect serves as both an engaging game and a powerful educational tool for future space explorers.
details:
How to Play Mission Architect (Simple Guide)

It’s a space game where you’re a mission architect: you pick a mission, build your spacecraft on a limited budget, then run the simulation and see whether it succeeds.

Stages in order

1. Opening screen

Wait for loading to finish, then click Start game.

2. Choose your mission

There are 3 missions, each with its own style:

Mission

Destination

Crew

Lunar Outpost

The Moon

Human astronauts

Martian Red Ridge

Mars

Robots only

Venus Flagship Explorer

Venus

Robots only

Each mission has 3 sub-tasks that give you science points. You can rotate the planet with your mouse or finger to look at it. Click Select on the mission you want.

3. Design your spacecraft (budget: $1,000,000)

  • Primary spacecraft (mandatory): you must pick all 3. They’re free and don’t use any of your budget.
  • Secondary systems (optional): things like a rover, a balloon, or small satellites. Each has a price. Click Buy to purchase, and click again to refund.

If you don’t have enough money left, the button gets disabled.

4. Crew

  • Moon: you must assign both astronauts.
  • Mars and Venus: no humans. You can add an AI Assistant / Drone module for free, or click Skip.

5. Spacesuits (Moon mission only)

Choose one suit (mandatory). You can also add safety gear and life-support systems with whatever budget remains.

6. Telemetry dashboard (the most important part)

The game calculates 4 meters from your choices, each out of 100:

  • Mass & volume: the heavier the spacecraft, the faster it burns fuel.
  • Crew efficiency: vehicles, equipment, and the AI assistant improve it.
  • Power: the power you generate must exceed the power you consume.
  • Radiation protection: higher is better.

Colors: green means 70 or more (good), orange means 40 to 69 (medium), and red means below 40 (weak).

You also receive a projected mission success rate, plus tips on what your weak points are.

7. Run the simulation

Click RUN MISSION SIMULATION to watch the countdown, launch, journey to the planet, and landing. If you’re in a hurry, click Skip to result.

8. Result

  • 75% or more: Success, and you earn the NASA Space Apps badge
  • 55% to 74%: Partial success
  • Below 55%: Failure

You’ll also see the science points you earned and the budget you have left.

Tips to win

  1. Select all three primary spacecraft, because you can’t continue without them.
  2. Don’t spend the whole budget: leftover money gives a small bonus to your success rate.
  3. Balance matters more than quantity: buying too much makes the spacecraft heavy, so pick items that raise the most meters.
  4. On Venus: you must buy the Aerobot balloon before the LLISSE lander, otherwise you lose 10% of your success rate.
  5. On the Moon: the Rover, the heavy thermal suit, and the Habitat make a big difference to crew efficiency and protection.
  6. If the result isn’t good, click Review meters to see your weak meter, or click Start over to begin again.
